question: What is the primary purpose of a gastrostomy feeding tube?

options.A: To deliver nutrition directly into the stomach
options.C: To bypass the small intestine during digestion
options.D: To remove excess air and fluid from the bowel

explanation: A gastrostomy tube places food and fluids straight into the stomach, bypassing the mouth and esophagus for patients who cannot swallow safely. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h1)

question: When is a gastrostomy tube usually chosen over a nasogastric tube?

options.A: When the patient only needs overnight hydration for a few days
options.B: When the patient is expected to resume normal eating within a week
options.C: When the stomach is surgically removed due to severe ulcer disease
options.D: When tube feeding is needed for longer than four to six weeks

explanation: Long-term enteral nutrition relies on gastrostomy tubes because they are more stable and comfortable than nasal tubes for extended use. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h1)

question: What makes a low-profile gastrostomy device different from a standard PEG tube?

options.A: It does not require an internal retention bolster or balloon
options.B: It delivers liquid nutrition directly into the large intestine
options.C: It sits flush against the skin without long dangling tubing
options.D: It is placed permanently and can never be removed or changed

explanation: Button-type low-profile devices are discreet and popular with active patients because they lack the long external tubing of standard PEG tubes. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why might a doctor choose a transjejunal feeding tube instead of a standard gastric tube?

options.A: To bypass the stomach entirely due to high aspiration risk
options.B: To provide a larger reservoir for liquid formula storage
options.C: To make daily stoma site cleaning much easier for caregivers
options.D: To allow the patient to chew and swallow food while feeding

explanation: Transjejunal tubes deliver nutrients further down into the small bowel, which helps prevent severe reflux and aspiration in vulnerable patients. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is the recommended head-of-bed elevation during a gastrostomy feeding?
explanation: Keeping the bed elevated between 30 and 45 degrees helps gravity keep formula in the stomach and prevents reflux into the airway. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h3)

question: A nurse is preparing to feed a patient via a PEG tube. What action should be performed first?

options.A: Flush the tube rapidly with 100 mL of cold water
options.B: Lie the patient completely flat to check the abdomen
options.C: Verify tube placement and assess bowel sounds
options.D: Attach the feeding bag and start the pump immediately

explanation: Safety checks like confirming tube position and ensuring active bowel sounds must always happen before introducing any fluid or formula. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which gastrostomy feeding method uses an electronic pump to deliver formula slowly over 24 hours?
explanation: Continuous feeding runs at a slow, steady hourly rate throughout the day and night using a mechanical pump. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is a major drawback of rapid bolus tube feedings?

options.A: They must run continuously for the entire day
options.B: They require expensive electronic pump machinery
options.C: They can cause nausea, cramping, and fullness
options.D: They completely eliminate normal bowel sounds

explanation: Pouring a large volume of formula into the stomach too fast overwhelms the organ, frequently leading to abdominal discomfort and vomiting. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why should a nurse gently rotate a PEG tube during routine stoma care?

options.A: To make sure the formula flows faster during meal times
options.B: To allow air to enter the stomach and reduce bloating
options.C: To prevent the internal bumper from sticking to the stomach wall
options.D: To help the external skin opening stretch wider for easier cleaning

explanation: Routine rotation stops tissue from growing over the internal retention bolster, preventing a serious complication called buried bumper syndrome. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which finding around a gastrostomy stoma site requires immediate reporting to the healthcare provider?

options.A: A small amount of dried crusting around the tubing
options.B: Purulent drainage and spreading skin redness
options.C: Mild pinkness that disappears after gentle cleaning
options.D: Normal skin tone matching the rest of the abdomen

explanation: Pus and spreading redness are classic signs of a localized infection that may require antibiotic treatment or adjusted wound care. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h5)

question: How much water should a nurse use to flush a gastrostomy tube between different medications?

options.D: No water should ever be used

explanation: Flushing with warm water between each medication clears residual drug from the tube and prevents dangerous chemical reactions or clogs. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h6)

question: A nurse has three different crushed pill medications to give a patient through a PEG tube. What is the correct way to administer them?

options.A: Mix all three crushed pills together in one large syringe of water
options.B: Give each medication separately with a water flush between them
options.C: Crush them together and push them down the dry tube all at once
options.D: Dissolve the pills directly into the hanging bag of liquid formula

explanation: Medications must never be mixed together in a single syringe to avoid drug interactions and severe tube blockage. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is the very first nursing action if a patient's gastrostomy tube accidentally falls out?

options.A: Pour sterile water directly into the exposed hole to keep it wet
options.B: Try to force a larger replacement tube into the opening immediately
options.C: Leave the open hole uncovered and wait for the doctor to arrive
options.D: Cover the stoma with a sterile dressing and call the provider

explanation: Gastrostomy tracts can begin to close within hours, so protecting the site and notifying the medical team urgently is vital to allow safe replacement. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h7)

question: Which complication is most directly prevented by flushing a gastrostomy tube regularly?

options.A: Allergic skin reactions to medical tape
options.B: Involuntary weight loss and muscle wasting
options.C: Severe lung infection caused by fluid aspiration
options.D: Tube occlusion from formula or pill residue

explanation: Regular water flushes clear out sticky nutritional formula and crushed medication particles before they dry and block the lumen. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is the most important infection control practice for a family caregiver managing a home gastrostomy tube?

options.A: Boiling all feeding bags in water after every single meal
options.B: Performing thorough hand hygiene before handling the tube
options.C: Cleaning the entire feeding pump machine with bleach daily
options.D: Wearing sterile surgical gloves for every single water flush

explanation: Proper handwashing is the single most effective way to prevent harmful bacteria from entering the gastrostomy site or formula bag. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h8)

question: Why is it important to have family caregivers demonstrate tube care before hospital discharge?

options.A: To legally transfer full liability for the medical device to the family
options.B: To confirm they can safely perform procedures and handle problems at home
options.C: To prove they do not need any further help from home health nurses
options.D: To test whether they can afford expensive commercial feeding pumps

explanation: Return demonstrations ensure that family members have practical competence and confidence to manage tube feedings safely without professional supervision. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h8)
